overfitting.explanation: Overfitting happens when a model learns the training data too well, including noise, so it performs poorly on new data.

revisions.explanation: Overfitting happens when a model memorises the training data instead of learning general patterns.
Overfitting happens when a model learns the training data too well, including noise, so it performs poorly on new unseen data. It is like memorizing answers instead of understanding the subject.

regularisation.explanation: Regularisation adds a penalty to prevent overfitting.

revisions.explanation: Regularisation helps prevent overfitting by adding a penalty term to the loss function.
Regularisation adds a penalty to the loss function to discourage complex models, helping prevent overfitting.

bias-variance tradeoff.explanation: The tradeoff between model simplicity (high bias) and model complexity (high variance).
